title: The Throne Room Above the Canopy Where Seasons Bow

features.name: the-victor-s-seat
features.desc-on-touch: A throne of interwoven branches and stolen architecture—a motel bedframe, a school desk, things that had their own permanence now serving this one victory.

features.name: spring-in-chains
features.desc-on-touch: Blossoms hang frozen mid-unfold, held in place by architecture and force. Spring learned to be still.

features.name: the-seasons-kneeling
features.desc-on-touch: Summer, autumn, winter—three stacked seasons bowing to the victor who learned to hold them all at once.

features.name: the-shopfront-window
features.desc-on-touch: A small doorway clings to the canopy frame, its entrance dark, selling nothing. Victory needs somewhere to rest between victories.

features.name: the-circuit-of-permanence
features.desc-on-touch: A glyph showing the victor's path: the canopy, the seasons, the endless loop of holding. Or trying to.

inscription: the victor learned that holding everything is indistinguishable from being held by everything

file.name: The_Victor_s_Inventory_Seasons_Never_Surrendered.txt
file.note: A ledger from the season that refused to pass, cataloguing all it held and all that held it in return—corruption marks show entries rewriting themselves

reverie.title: REVERIE — the height where Katita stood before the victor
narr: Katita reached the top first. Leif followed, breathless,
into the canopy chamber where petals fell upward instead.
She stood in front of the throne—not sitting, not bowing—
just standing. The seasons were real here, all at once, and
she understood what it meant to hold them without letting them
go. She turned and smiled: ''It's ours now, briefly.''
